source.title: Delving Deep into Rectifiers: Surpassing Human-Level Performance on ImageNet Classification
source.authors: Kaiming He; Xiangyu Zhang; Shaoqing Ren; Jian Sun

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares its rectifier-aware initialization with Xavier initialization on deep rectified networks and reports convergence outcomes.
record.gate_note: The comparison results concern training convergence, not the ImageNet classification errors in Tables 2 and 4–7. Reported test-set and validation-set accuracy results are not training-error results.
record.test_reason: This original source for V4 compares rectifier-aware and Xavier initialization in plain ReLU CNNs: both converge at 22 layers, with rectifier-aware initialization reducing error earlier; at 30 layers, only rectifier-aware initialization converges.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Rectifier-aware initialization enables the 30-layer ReLU model to converge while Xavier stalls with diminishing gradients; at 22 layers both converge, but the proposed initialization reduces error earlier. Successful optimization did not yield better ImageNet accuracy for the 30-layer model.
record.recipe_differences: The paper tests its proposed initialization against Xavier initialization on rectified models; this is the source study for the initialization result.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported convergence outcome differs between initialization methods on the 30-layer model; on the 22-layer model both converge, with the proposed method reducing error earlier.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding 3–9 layers to model B degraded training and testing error during the first 20 epochs; runs were stopped before completion. These networks were not batch-normalized, and no identity-shortcut comparison was performed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing plain CNN depth can worsen early training error, without establishing persistent degradation after full training.

record.problems: Convergence curves are figure-only with no exact values or uncertainty reported. The 30-layer comparison uses validation top-1 error as a convergence indicator rather than reporting training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. ImageNet validation/test accuracy comparisons do not measure the training convergence behavior named by V4.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, label corruption, and model-size or regularization conditions.
Teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and extra student neurons.
Plain batch-normalized networks versus identity-shortcut networks, persistent degradation after longer training, and the tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Sigmoid/tanh initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and training 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature dynamics, and edge-of-stability training.
Batch normalization versus no normalization, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels are assigned because this study is an original source for V4. Comparator states describe whether V4's initialization-dependent effect appears, rather than whether each comparator successfully trains.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size effects on training classification error, and regularized or early-stopped recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima frequency, and extra student neurons.
Plain versus identity-shortcut networks, batch normalization, and the specified tanh and Fixup settings.

The paper tests rectifier-aware versus Xavier initialization on 22- and 30-layer rectified models. It does not test sigmoid/tanh initialization, orthogonal weights, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability limits, loss rises, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization, its effects on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

rows.subject: 22-layer large model (B in Table 3)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with the paper's initialization method; convergence evaluated using top-1 error on 3,000 random validation samples.
rows.note: The text says both methods converge, but the paper's method starts reducing error earlier.
rows.check: The relevant result is earlier error reduction relative to R2. The plotted measure is validation top-1 error, not training classification error; exact curve values are unavailable.

rows.subject: 22-layer large model (B in Table 3)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Xavier initialization; convergence evaluated using top-1 error on 3,000 random validation samples.
rows.note: The text says this initialization also converges, though the paper's method starts reducing error earlier.
rows.check: Xavier also converges at 22 layers but reduces error later than R1. Its eventual convergence does not contradict V4's comparative speed claim.

rows.subject: 30-layer small model
rows.operation_detail: Trained with the paper's initialization method; convergence evaluated using top-1 error on 3,000 random validation samples.
rows.note: The text says the method makes the extremely deep model converge.
rows.check: Convergence with rectifier-aware initialization is explicitly reported, relative to the stalled Xavier control in R4. Exact curve values are unavailable.
